sections.body: Scientists PREDICT (make a smart guess), then TEST to find out.
A fair test changes only ONE thing. Everything else stays the same.
Example: Which ball bounces highest? Drop each from the SAME height onto the SAME floor. Only the ball changes.
Predict which paper aeroplane design flies furthest. Throw each the same way and measure!
Ask 'What do you think will happen?' before every experiment. It's fine to be wrong. That's how science works!

quiz.q: Testing which ball bounces highest, what should stay the SAME?
options: The height you drop it from
hints: We are testing the balls, so the ball changes.
Racing toy cars fairly, you'd start them on the same slope. What's 'the same' when dropping balls?
quiz.explain: Drop each ball from the same height so the test is fair.

hints: It's what you THINK will happen.
'I think the ice will melt in 10 minutes' is said before watching. What's that called?
quiz.explain: A prediction is a smart guess about what will happen.

quiz.q: Kai tests which paper plane flies furthest. To be fair, what should change?
hints: A fair test changes just ONE thing.
What is Kai trying to find out about?
Testing which ball bounces highest, only the ball changes. The height stays the same.
quiz.explain: Kai is testing planes, so only the plane changes. He throws each one the same way.
